p: MyShaf is not a separate code base. It is the Sharia flavour of the GENFI code in agent_tools/ of bravo-agency-app. The same Dart files build both apps. 37 isSharia() branches in 7 files decide what differs, 26 of them in router.dart. Everything on Genfi mobile app assessment applies to MyShaf. This page covers only what is different, and it leads to one decision that should be made before any engineering work on MyShaf.

li.p: Almost nobody uses it. Datadog RUM recorded 12 MyShaf sessions in the last 30 days, all Android, all version 1.3.1. GENFI 1.16.0 recorded 238,470 sessions in the same window. The RUM sampling rate for MyShaf is a GitHub variable we could not read, so the true number may be higher, but not by the three orders of magnitude needed to match GENFI.

No release for four months. The last MyShaf tag is v1.3.1-beta.15-myshaf (19 Jun 2026). Since then agent_tools received 135 commits and the shared packages 52, shipped to GENFI in 75 tags. None of those commits mention Sharia. The next MyShaf build will carry four months of change that nobody has run in the Sharia flavour.

CI has never worked for MyShaf. The SIT pipeline ran 24 times since January 2026 and failed every time. The prod pipeline ran 8 times and failed every time, the last three at the Play Store upload step after the iOS job succeeded. The UAT pipeline has never run. The builds in the stores came from somewhere else, most likely a laptop.

No test runs the Sharia flavour. The flavour is a compile-time --dart-define=FLAVOUR. Of 149 test files, none sets a Sharia flavour. The Sharia screens, routes and the device-integrity flow are untested.

Prod environments are unprotected (verified). The GENFI page could not read this. On 26 Oct 2026 the GitHub API shows zero protection rules on sharia_prod_myshaf and on the other seven sharia_* environments.

Telemetry is weaker than GENFI's. Crashlytics is not wired for the Sharia flavours at Gradle level and is skipped in main.dart. Firebase Analytics collection is only enabled when the flavour is convent, so the analytics wrapper sends nothing for MyShaf. Datadog RUM is on. MyShaf is the only flavour with a device-integrity check (Play Integrity / App Attest), behind a one-flag Remote Config model that defaults to on.

Decision first. GENFI's open question 6 ("does MyShaf stay a flavour or become its own app") has a third answer: retire it. With 12 sessions a month, the cost of keeping a second flavour green through the GENFI roadmap is hard to justify. See the Options section.

p: The risk is not that MyShaf is broken today. The store binary is frozen. The risk is the next release: four months of GENFI changes in shared screens (feature/prospect, feature/common, the router) reach Sharia users through a pipeline that has never been green, with no test and no cohort rollout for this flavour.
Shared with GENFI and SQUARE (secret-printing workflows, keystore artifact, BRAVO_GCP_SA_KEY in 51 repos): see Genfi mobile app assessment and Agency phase 0: Close the leak. Specific to MyShaf:

li.p: sharia_prod_myshaf has no protection rule (verified). The manual-approval step is the only gate, and agent_tools_prod_release_build.yaml shows how a _build variant can bypass such a step.
SIT builds are unpinned (SHA_256_FINGERPRINT not passed). Testers never exercise pinning before UAT.
FEATURE_ENABLE_PROXY and FEATURE_JAILBREAK_DETECTION enter prod from GitHub variables. A changed variable changes the security posture of a prod build without a code review.
Secrets interpolated into run: commands in all three MyShaf workflows.
The device-integrity check defaults to on but is a Remote Config flag (FEATURE_INTEGRITY_CHECK). Anyone with Remote Config access can turn it off for every user. Decide whether that is intended.
The signed prod AAB and IPA are uploaded as workflow artifacts for 1 day. That is how a release can be published by hand when the upload step fails, and it is also an exfiltration path.

p: Three options for what MyShaf becomes. Pick one before planning engineering work.

td.p: A. Retire MyShaf, move Sharia agents into GENFI
Sharia products become a product line inside GENFI (the shared packages already model them as data). Store listing closed after a migration window.
Removes a flavour nobody tests, a second store presence, three pipelines and 37 branches. The GENFI roadmap then has one app to keep green.
Needs a product and Sharia-business decision, user migration, and a check of any regulatory reason for a separate Sharia app.
B. Keep the flavour, make it a first-class release train
MyShaf ships on every GENFI release train. CI repaired, Sharia flavour in the parity net, cohort rollout per flavour, Crashlytics and analytics decided.
No user migration. The code stays one.
Every GENFI step on the roadmap gets a MyShaf row. Doubles the test matrix for 12 sessions a month.
No new releases. Store listing stays. Fix only security items that affect the frozen binary (none found in the binary itself).
The binary ages against backend and OS changes. A forced release later carries all the drift at once.

p: Recommended: A, subject to the product check in open question 2. If the answer is that Sharia agents must have a separate app, then B, and the first step is to repair CI and add the flavour to the parity net before any other change reaches MyShaf.
Until the decision: do not release MyShaf from the current master. If a release is unavoidable, build from v1.3.1-beta.15-myshaf plus cherry-picked fixes.
